# Sirach Chapter 40 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 40 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_040_page_001.jpg

---

40:1 Every human being carries a heavy burden. From the day we leave the womb to the day we return to the earth that is mother to us all, we live under a heavy yoke of toil.

40:2 Confusion and anxiety, dread of what lies ahead, and the day of death —

40:3 these touch everyone, from the person sitting on a throne of glory to the one crouched in the dust and ashes,

40:4 from the one dressed in royal purple and a crown to the one wrapped in rough sackcloth —

40:5 anger, envy, trouble, restlessness, the constant fear of death, rage, quarrels. And when a person finally lies down to rest, the night only confuses the mind further.

40:6 Sleep brings little peace. As in a night watch, the heart is troubled: sometimes a terrifying nightmare, sometimes sinking into a stupor — with only brief relief, like a soldier who has just survived a battle.

40:7 He wakes up, astonished to find there was nothing to be frightened of after all.

40:8 Every creature goes through this — human and animal alike. But for sinners it's seven times worse.

40:9 Death, bloodshed, conflict, the sword, disaster, famine, destruction, disease —

40:10 all of this was made on account of the wicked. The Flood itself came because of them.

40:11 Whatever comes from the earth, returns to the earth. Whatever comes from the water returns to the sea.

40:12 Every bribe and every crooked act will eventually be wiped out. But integrity endures forever.

40:13 A corrupt person's wealth dries up like a desert stream and disappears like a crack of thunder.

40:14 The generous person will flourish; but those who act dishonestly will collapse completely.

40:15 The children of the godless won't put down strong roots — they're like plants on bare rock.

40:16 The reeds by every riverbank get pulled up before anything else.

40:17 But kindness is like a garden of paradise, and generous giving lasts forever.

40:18 A simple, self-sufficient life has its sweetness — but finding a treasure is better still.

40:19 Having children and building a city keeps your name alive — but finding wisdom is better still. Herds and vineyards make you prosperous — but a wife you truly love is better still.

40:20 Wine and music lift the heart — but loving wisdom is better still.

40:21 A flute and a harp make beautiful sounds — but a beautiful voice is better still.

40:22 The eye delights in elegance and beauty — but seeing the fresh green of new grain is better still.

40:23 A friend or companion is always welcome — but a husband and wife together are better still.

40:24 Family and helpers get you through hard times — but giving generously to others does it even better.

40:25 Gold and silver give you stability — but good advice is better still.

40:26 Wealth and strength give you confidence — but the fear of the Lord surpasses them both. When you fear the Lord, you lack nothing; there is no need to look elsewhere.

40:27 The fear of the Lord is like paradise — it covers you with more glory than any roof overhead.

40:28 My child, don't live the life of a beggar. Better to die than to beg.

40:29 When you depend on another person's table to survive, that's not really living. You debase yourself by eating food that isn't yours — but the wise and disciplined person knows better than to end up there.

40:30 The shameless person finds begging sweet enough in the moment — but it burns like fire in the belly.
